title: BRAKES CROSS CHANNEL FAULT on the Engine and Warning Display

ata.title: Wheels and Brakes — Brake Control Unit

abstract: Fault isolation for a cross channel disagreement between the two brake and steering control units, which most often follows a software or brake standard mismatch rather than a hardware failure.

sections.purpose: This procedure isolates the cause of a brake control cross channel disagreement. Use it when the warning is displayed in flight or on the ground, and after any control unit or brake assembly change.
sections.fault_description: The two control units continuously compare their computed brake demand and their measured pressure at every position. A disagreement beyond the comparison tolerance for longer than two seconds raises the warning and reverts the affected position to the alternate braking mode. In service the great majority of these events are configuration rather than hardware: a unit loaded with a parameter set that does not match the brake standard fitted, or a mixed pair of units after a partial replacement. The built in test code table below resolves the cockpit message to a position and a channel. The fault is latched until the next power-up and is recorded with the position identity in the maintenance store.
sections.isolation_procedure: Read the maintenance store and record the fault code and the position identity. Resolve the code against the built in test code table and note the channel it points to. Read the software part numbers reported by both units and compare them; if they differ, load the correct standard to both units and repeat the brake control system test. If they are the same, compare the loaded parameter set against the brake standard fitted at the reported position using the pairing table. Where the pairing is wrong, load the correct parameter set and repeat the test. Where the pairing is correct, do a continuity check on the pressure transducer harness at the reported position and measure the insulation resistance of the hose run at FIN 2GM2. Where the harness is sound, exchange the two control units between their positions and repeat the test; if the fault follows the unit, replace it, and if it stays at the position, the fault is in the aircraft wiring or in the brake. Where the brake is suspected, do the wear and pressure check at that position before removal.
sections.dispatch_note: Despatch is permitted with one control unit inoperative and the affected positions in the alternate braking mode, subject to a landing distance penalty. Despatch is not permitted with a cross channel fault that has not been isolated, because the fault does not identify which of the two computed demands is correct.

type_data.fault_symptom: BRAKES CROSS CHANNEL FAULT displayed on the engine and warning display

possible_causes.cause: Parameter set does not match the brake heat stack standard fitted at the position
Mixed control unit software standard after a partial replacement
Pressure transducer harness open or high resistance at the reported position

dispatch.dispatch_condition: One control unit inoperative, affected positions in alternate braking mode, landing distance penalty applied

issue.reason: Built in test code table split per control unit standard and the unit part number read as the first step of the procedure.

ata.title: Wheels and Brakes — Brake Control Unit

abstract: Fault isolation for a cross channel disagreement between the two brake and steering control units, resolved against the built in test code table for the unit standard fitted, which most often follows a software or brake standard mismatch rather than a hardware failure.

sections.purpose: This procedure isolates the cause of a brake control cross channel disagreement. Use it when the warning is displayed in flight or on the ground, and after any control unit or brake assembly change. Read the control unit part number first; the built in test code table is stated per unit standard and the same cockpit message resolves differently on the two.
sections.fault_description: The two control units continuously compare their computed brake demand and their measured pressure at every position. A disagreement beyond the comparison tolerance for longer than two seconds raises the warning and reverts the affected position to the alternate braking mode. In service the great majority of these events are configuration rather than hardware: a unit loaded with a parameter set that does not match the brake standard fitted, or a mixed pair of units after a partial replacement. The requalified unit runs the same operational software over a different device family and does not emit three of the codes the original table depends on, so the code table is stated per unit standard and the wrong table will send the mechanic to a channel that is not at fault. The fault is latched until the next power-up and is recorded with the position identity in the maintenance store.
sections.isolation_procedure: Read the part number of the control unit at each position and select the built in test code table for the standard fitted; on a mixed pair, use the table of the unit that reported. Read the maintenance store and record the fault code and the position identity, and resolve the code against the table selected. Where the code is not listed in the table for the standard fitted, do not fall back to the other table: treat the event as a mixed pair and read the software part numbers reported by both units. Where the software standards differ, load the correct standard to both units and repeat the brake control system test. Where they are the same, compare the loaded parameter set against the brake standard fitted at the reported position using the pairing table. Where the pairing is wrong, load the correct parameter set and repeat the test. Where the pairing is correct, do a continuity check on the pressure transducer harness at the reported position and measure the insulation resistance of the hose run at FIN 2GM2. Where the harness is sound, exchange the two control units between their positions and repeat the test; if the fault follows the unit, replace it, and if it stays at the position, the fault is in the aircraft wiring or in the brake. Where the brake is suspected, do the wear and pressure check at that position before removal.
sections.dispatch_note: Despatch is permitted with one control unit inoperative and the affected positions in the alternate braking mode, subject to a landing distance penalty. Despatch is not permitted with a cross channel fault that has not been isolated, because the fault does not identify which of the two computed demands is correct.

Parameter set does not match the brake heat stack standard fitted at the position
Mixed control unit software standard after a partial replacement
Pressure transducer harness open or high resistance at the reported position
